item.title: Oro selected as pilot for PH Human Rights Plan
item.description: CAGAYAN de Oro has been selected as one of 10 pilot areas nationwide for the localization of the 4th Philippine Human Rights Plan (PHRP4), a 2024–2028 roadmap that integrates rights-based approaches into governance and inclusive development. item.description: When bombs hit the transmitter of Radio Veritas in Bulacan in February 1986, the main independent source of information during the uprising suddenly went silent. But the broadcast did not end. It moved underground. item.title: Price hikes if Agus-Pulangi Hydro Complex is privatized: Consumer group
item.description: A Mindanao consumer advocacy group is raising concerns that privatizing the Agus–Pulangi Hydroelectric Complex could lead to higher electricity rates and reduced public oversight of one of the region’s most critical energy assets. item.description: Pag-IBIG Fund highlighted the role of public-private partnerships and modern construction technology in accelerating socialized housing delivery as officials joined President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. in the ceremonial launch of a precast manufacturing facility in Taytay, Rizal on Monday, Feb. 16. item.title: 16 Lanao royal houses set grand congress, name 2026 leaders
item.description: ILIGAN CITY — The 16 Royal Houses of Lanao, the highest traditional authority of the Lanao Sultanate, are set to convene the Lanao Sultanate Grand Congress alongside the 2026 induction of officers, a gathering aimed at strengthening unity and reinforcing the role of traditional leadership in peace-building and cultural preservation. item.title: Fall of ‘Bongwaco,’ ‘Rhedda’ may end NPA in Normin
item.description: CAMP EVANGELISTA, Cagayan de Oro — The military says communist insurgency in Northern Mindanao and Caraga may be nearing its end, with only two senior leaders of the New People's Army (NPA) still at large following the death of a key commander in Agusan del Sur.
